title: Strings and f-strings
content:
What problem does this solve?
You often need to build readable messages that mix text with live values — a status line, battle log, or inventory note.

Basic syntax
  f"Health: {health}"

What actually happens
An f-string is evaluated at runtime. Python finds each {expression}, evaluates it, converts the result to text, and inserts it into the surrounding string.

This is clearer than concatenating many pieces with + because the template stays readable.
concepts: f-strings start with f before the opening quote
Expressions inside {} are evaluated and embedded
Prefer f-strings for formatted messages once you know the values' names

examples.title: Character status line
examples.explanation: Python substitutes the current values of name and health into the string.

common_mistakes: Forgetting the leading f — then {health} prints literally
Putting quotes incorrectly inside the braces

exercises.title: Formatted character card
exercises.prompt:
Create variables name="Selene", health=90, level=5.
Print exactly one line:
Selene - Level 5 - HP 90

Use an f-string.
exercises.starter_code:
name = "Selene"
health = 90
level = 5
# Print the formatted summary
hints: Start your string with f and put expressions in braces.
Keep the hyphens and spaces exactly as shown in the required line.

exercises.title: Predict the f-string
hints: Substitute the braced expressions with their values.
Keep the surrounding words and spaces exactly.
